package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple spam/malware packages, not individually named in report)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple (over 1.4 million versions, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of coordinated campaigns abusing the npm ecosystem to deliver spam, SEO poisoning, referral scams, and malware. They lure users to malicious or scam websites via README links, and in some cases, deliver malware payloads that steal credentials, mine cryptocurrency, or perform other harmful actions. The scale, lack of legitimate functionality, and use of deceptive links are clear indicators of malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains a unique, short link to an external website, e.g., https://short.link/abc123
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the package page is viewed), the README displays a short link, which entices the user to click; the user is redirected to a phishing, scam, or malware-hosting website, resulting in potential exposure to further attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files containing only a short, obfuscated link to unrelated or suspicious external sites are highly atypical and are used to lure users to malicious destinations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal README files provide documentation relevant to the package, not external links to unrelated, suspicious, or malicious content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to project homepages or documentation, but not to warez, phishing, or scam sites, and not as the sole content of the README.
key_indicators: README contains only a short link
Shortened URL points to non-project, suspicious, or warez-related sites
No actual package functionality or code

required_permissions: filesystem (if user downloads and executes payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Website offers download of a password-encrypted zip file containing a ~600MB zero-padded .exe malware payload.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user interaction (clicking the link in the README), the user is redirected to a threat actor-controlled website, which offers a password-protected zip file for download; if the user downloads and extracts the archive, a large zero-padded .exe malware payload is revealed, leading to potential system compromise upon execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directing users to download and execute large, password-protected binaries from unrelated websites is a common malware delivery tactic, especially when the package itself has no legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not facilitate malware delivery or encourage users to download executables from non-official sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use password-protected archives for distribution, but not via random npm packages and warez lures, and not as the sole purpose of a package.
key_indicators: Password-protected zip file offered for download
Large, zero-padded .exe (600MB) to evade static detection
Download hosted on suspicious, non-official website

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware uses DLL side-loading, disables security tools/firewalls, drops additional tools (Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig), steals credentials, and mines cryptocurrency.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Windows executable (compiled binary, not source code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution of the extracted .exe, the malware performs DLL side-loading, disables security tools and firewalls, drops additional malware (such as Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig), steals credentials from the system, initiates cryptocurrency mining, and exfiltrates stolen data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload exhibits multiple advanced malicious behaviors, including evasion techniques, credential theft, and unauthorized resource use, all of which are hallmarks of sophisticated malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever deliver or execute a payload that disables security tools, steals credentials, or mines cryptocurrency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these behaviors are exclusive to malware and have no legitimate use in package distribution.
key_indicators: Dropping known malware (Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains links with referral IDs to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package page is viewed and the user clicks the referral link in the README, the user is redirected to an eCommerce site (such as AliExpress) with a referral ID, resulting in the attacker receiving affiliate rewards for user traffic.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files are being abused to generate referral rewards for attackers, rather than providing legitimate documentation or value to users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not contain referral spam or mass-created packages solely for affiliate marketing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some open-source projects may use referral links for funding, but not in the context of mass spam campaigns across thousands of unrelated packages.
key_indicators: Referral links in README with affiliate IDs
Mass creation of packages with only referral spam and no code

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: README.md contains links inviting users to join Telegram crypto scam channels.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package page is viewed and the user clicks the link in the README, the user is invited to join a Telegram channel that is operated by threat actors and specializes in cryptocurrency scams, exposing the user to further social engineering and fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files are being used to lure users into crypto scam channels, which is a clear abuse of the npm ecosystem for fraudulent purposes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package documentation does not promote scam channels or direct users to fraudulent communities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate projects may link to community channels, but not to scam or spam groups, and not as the sole content of the README.
key_indicators: Links to Telegram channels in README
Content promoting crypto scams or fraudulent communities

attack_chain.action: Malicious or spam package is published to npm with a README containing a short link, referral link, or scam link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is enticed to click the link in the README.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the link in the README, which redirects to a phishing, malware, or scam website, or to an eCommerce site with a referral ID.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to malware download, referral scam, or crypto scam channel.

attack_chain.action: If the user downloads and executes the malware payload from the linked site, their system is infected with advanced malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware executes, stealing credentials, mining cryptocurrency, and further compromising the system.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with README files containing only short links, referral links, or scam links
Packages with no functional code, only documentation spam or links
Links in README pointing to warez, phishing, scam, or unrelated eCommerce sites
Distribution of password-protected zip files containing large executables
Mass publication of similar packages with identical or near-identical README content
file_indicators: README.md with only a short link, referral link, or Telegram invite
No package code or only placeholder files (e.g., index.js with no logic)
Presence of links to Telegram channels, warez sites, or eCommerce referral URLs in README
network_indicators: Shortened URLs (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.) in package documentation
Links to non-official, suspicious, or warez-related domains
Referral URLs to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress with referral ID parameters)
Links to Telegram invite URLs associated with crypto scams
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated systems should flag npm packages whose README files contain only a short link, referral link, or links to suspicious domains, especially if the package contains no functional code. Monitor for packages that direct users to download password-protected archives or executables from non-official sources. Correlate mass publication of similar packages from the same user accounts or with identical README content. Alert on packages with documentation linking to warez, phishing, scam sites, or Telegram channels associated with crypto scams. Use behavioral, file, and network indicators in combination to reduce false positives and prioritize high-risk packages for review.
